articles.title: There Is No Firewall for a Sentence
articles.excerpt: Written by: Josh Greenwell Staff Applied AI Engineer This blog article is a condensed version of our whitepaper on securing AI agents against prompt injection. The full paper includes the appendices o…
articles.body: Written by: Josh Greenwell Staff Applied AI Engineer This blog article is a condensed version of our whitepaper on securing AI agents against prompt injection. The full paper includes the appendices on prompt-injection defenses and the complete reference list. You can download the original pdf format here . Introduction When we started seriously hardening LuumenAI , the question I kept turning over was some version of "how am I going to secure this thing." For a while I treated it like a normal hardening problem and went looking for the control I had missed. There mostly is not one. You cannot secure a language model the way that question assumes, and the sooner that sinks in, the sooner you can work on the parts that are actually fixable.
articles.author: serene

articles.title: 39 screenshots and not one useful name, so a local Gemma names them for me
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady slothshot renames screenshots after what's in them. Screenshot 2026-10-03 at 08.15.44.png becomes 2026-10-03…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built slothshot renames screenshots after what's in them. Screenshot 2026-10-03 at 08.15.44.png becomes 2026-10-03 railbook-e-ticket-pnr-4421907736.png . My screenshots folder had 39 files in three naming schemes, because they came over from a Linux laptop: Screenshot from 2026-02-17 19-14-51.png , 2026-04-09_01-26-24.png and the macOS Screenshot 2026-10-17 at 13.34.06.png . None of them said what was in the picture. When I needed one, I opened thumbnails until I found it. Renaming them by hand would fix that, and I was never going to do it. So now a vision model on my laptop looks at each screenshot and picks a name: the app or site, and the specific thing on screen.

articles.excerpt: Notes from a 2 AM On-Call: Why Our vLLM Semantic Router Dropped 40% of Requests Under Load The Failure Symptom 2024-03-15 02:17:43 WARNING: Route decision timeout after 5000ms 2024-03-15 02:17:48 ERRO…
articles.body: Notes from a 2 AM On-Call: Why Our vLLM Semantic Router Dropped 40% of Requests Under Load The Failure Symptom 2024-03-15 02:17:43 WARNING: Route decision timeout after 5000ms 2024-03-15 02:17:48 ERROR: 127 requests dropped (no route assigned) 2024-03-15 02:18:12 INFO: QPS: 240 → 140 (41% degradation) Our FastAPI gateway wrapping vllm-project/semantic-router started silently dropping requests at 2 AM during a traffic spike. No 5xx errors, no OOM kills, just requests vanishing into the void. Prometheus showed route decision latency climbing from 80ms to 4.8 seconds, then requests just disappeared from logs entirely.

articles.title: I'm making a one-bullet puzzle game on my own. Here's what changed after players got their hands on it.
articles.excerpt: I'm the only developer on Bloop. Design, code, UI, levels and the store pages are all me. It's a mobile puzzle game where you get one bullet per level: pull back, bank it off the walls, and pop every…
articles.body: I'm the only developer on Bloop. Design, code, UI, levels and the store pages are all me. It's a mobile puzzle game where you get one bullet per level: pull back, bank it off the walls, and pop every Bloop on the screen with that one shot. It's live on Google Play and the App Store now, with 300 levels. It's also still a work in progress. This is what changed since the early versions, and why. The first question Before menus, ads or a single extra level, the first build had one job: answer "is shooting one bullet satisfying?" The aim preview and the real bullet use the exact same path code, so if the preview says the bullet goes there, it goes there. In a one-shot game, a preview that lies even slightly feels like cheating.
articles.author: Rahim Khan

articles.title: 3.2 Million Redis and 1.9 Million MongoDB Services: The Steady Background of Exposed Data Stores
articles.excerpt: 3.2 Million Redis and 1.9 Million MongoDB Services: The Steady Background of Exposed Data Stores Month after month, the same services appear in internet scan data at the same order of magnitude: Redis…
articles.body: 3.2 Million Redis and 1.9 Million MongoDB Services: The Steady Background of Exposed Data Stores Month after month, the same services appear in internet scan data at the same order of magnitude: Redis in the millions, MongoDB in the millions, and a long tail of databases below them. These are not new vulnerabilities. They are a persistent configuration outcome, and they deserve a place in any account of enterprise exposure that goes beyond patching. The scale ZoomEye queries run on 20 October 2026 with sub_type="all" and a page size of one record returned: Query Matched assets service="redis" 3,207,842 service="mongodb" 1,923,240 service="ldap" 1,089,053 service="ssh" 166,939,313 service="rdp" 16,527,336 These counts describe services that answered on a scanned port.

articles.excerpt: Hey everyone 👋, If you’re building AI apps today, you probably know the headache of API fragmentation. You might want to use GPT-4o for reasoning, Claude 3.5 for coding, and Llama 3 for fast, cheap p…
articles.body: Hey everyone 👋, If you’re building AI apps today, you probably know the headache of API fragmentation. You might want to use GPT-4o for reasoning, Claude 3.5 for coding, and Llama 3 for fast, cheap processing. But doing this currently means: ❌ Managing 5+ different provider accounts. ❌ Rewriting code to match different SDKs. ❌ Dealing with separate billing, rate limits, and declined cards. ❌ App downtime when a provider's server crashes. I am validating an idea for a Unified LLM API Gateway to solve this. It acts as a single proxy between your code and 40+ AI providers (250+ models). How it works: Drop-in Replacement: 100% compatible with the OpenAI SDK. Just change the baseURL and API key. Zero code rewrites.

articles.title: Mastering Asynchronous Reconciliation: How to Keep Your Financial Ledgers In Sync Without Losing Your Mind
articles.excerpt: If you have ever built a modern fintech application, SaaS billing platform, or e-commerce engine, you already know a dirty little secret of software engineering: money does not move instantly. In a sy…
articles.body: If you have ever built a modern fintech application, SaaS billing platform, or e-commerce engine, you already know a dirty little secret of software engineering: money does not move instantly. In a synchronous, closed-loop software architecture, state transitions are a walk in the park. When a user transfers funds within a single monolithic application, your database transaction commits instantly, and the glorious invariant that debits must equal credits is preserved atomically. But the real world outside your clean PostgreSQL database is chaotic, latency-laden, and fundamentally distributed.

articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.excerpt: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attac…
articles.body: Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild. Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin. The flaws at issue are present in PHP , the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal , Magento , Joomla and WordPress . Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server.
